messages:
sophie (support): Heads up - large customer (Shopr) just escalated: sporadic 5xx + long tail p99s (~20-30s) on hosted inference for model-x-prod. They attached traces and a small repro. They say it started ~90m ago.

mike (oncall): copying traces now. timeline? any config changes? :eyes:

sophie (support): Customer reports: API returns 502/504 and then after ~20s a successful response. They provided request ids: req_9f2a, req_9f2b, req_9f2c. Happening on region us-west-2. No token/auth issues.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-88 (trigger: hosted-api-5xx-spike). Pager duty notified.

kai (eng-sre): I pulled the logs for those req ids. seeing queue wait times ~18-22s before worker pickup. gateway logs: 
```
gateway: request_id=req_9f2a wait_ms=19876 queue_depth=102 max_queue=100 action=early_reject=false
runtime: batcher_latency_ms=18000 KVCacheHit=false
```
Looks like queue depth hit the configured limit and continuous batching backlog piled up.

jordan (runtime): Oh interesting. continuous-batching window tuned wide for model-x to improve throughput; if throughput bursts, queue depth can pile up. What is tenant-level queue cap?

kai (eng-sre): tenant max_queue_depth for hosted currently 100 for that plan. We see spikes to 102 then requests waiting. Some requests still accepted and eventually served after huge batch build. p95 still OK but p99 explodes.

lena (product): Customer complaining about user-facing latency. Can we offer immediate mitigation while we dig?

mike (oncall): Immediate mitigations I can try: 1) reduce continuous batching window for model-x-prod, 2) temporarily reject new requests above a lower threshold to shed load, 3) fallback to smaller model-x-small. Which is safest?

jordan (runtime): I'd prefer reducing batch window and lowering max_queue_depth to force faster dispatch. fallback to smaller model may change quality. We should avoid silent rejects.

skilled bot message from deploy-bot: autoscaler triggered scale_up for model-x-prod nodepool (+2 gpus) at 08:45UTC.

kai (eng-sre): Dashboard snapshots: request_queue_depth (hosted/model-x-prod) shows 5m spike to 110 at 08:42, backlog_duration histogram tail at 22s. Batcher build_time distribution centered at 18s during spike.

sophie (support): Customer asks for repro steps. They gave a small load generator curl: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"long prompt ..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done
```
They run ~50 concurrents from single IP.

mike (oncall): I can repro locally in staging by running similar concurrent calls. Observed same queue buildup.

jordan (runtime): Quick config change I'm going to push to hosted runtime for that model: reduce continuous_batch_window_ms from 20000 -> 5000 and max_queue_depth from 100 -> 60 for that tenant namespace. This will prioritize latency. Will roll canary 1 host then 5.

kai (eng-sre): Also enabling tenant-level circuit-breaker to return 429 when queue_depth >= 60 so we fail fast instead of long waits. We'll add a header X-Queue-Dropped so client knows.

lena (product): Please notify customer about planned mitigations and expected UX changes (more 429s but much quicker failures). We should offer rate-limits guidance.

sophie (support): Sending message to Shopr: short note with two options: reduce concurrency or accept temporary 429s while we lower batch window. They prefer not to change client immediately.

mike (oncall): Rolling canary now. patch: 
```
PATCH /runtime/configs/model-x-prod
{ "continuous_batch_window_ms":5000, "max_queue_depth":60 }
```
Monitoring p99 and queue_depth.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: config/model-x-prod v12 -> v13 (canary 1/10)

kai (eng-sre): After canary we see queue_depth drop and backlog duration p99 from 22s -> 5s. no 5xx in canary logs.

mike (oncall): Rolling to 3/10 now.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: hosted-api-5xx-spike for canary hosts.

jordan (runtime): Full rollout completed. configuration applied across region us-west-2. Immediate customer impact: reduced latency, but expect some 429s for high-concurrency attempts.

sophie (support): Shopr confirms reduced p99 and no more 502/504s after our changes. They're seeing a few 429s but prefer that vs long waits. They asked for postmortem and whether we can tune for them.

kai (eng-sre): Next steps for root cause: 1) investigate why continuous batching window allowed such long build times under that workload (request size, token lengths). 2) evaluate adaptive batch windowing by request size. 3) consider tenant queue autoscaling or reserved capacity for high-throughput customers.

lena (product): Also capture guidance in docs: recommended concurrency per plan, sample client-side backoff, and rate-limits for hosted.

mike (oncall): I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. will open a postmortem and tag platform-rls and runtime.

sophie (support): Customer happy with temporary fix. They've requested RCA and a config change for their dedicated plan to avoid this in future.

jordan (runtime): Logging snippet I'm adding to gateway to better surface queue wait reason: 
```
log_extra: { "queue_depth":${qd}, "batch_window_ms":${bw}, "batch_size":${bs} }
```
This will help future triage.

kai (eng-sre): Recording repro steps in incident doc: use the curl loop with 40-60 concurrency, each payload ~1k tokens, region us-west-2, model-x-prod. Repro in staging with same config.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421-88 will remain open for monitoring and RCA artifacts.

mike (oncall): Thanks team. If anyone sees recurrence ping #eng-oncall. I'll drop followup notes in the incident board. :thumbsup:

sophie (support): Closing loop with Shopr and offering one week of dedicated capacity trial. They accepted. I'll follow up with legal for contract path.

lena (product): Filing a ticket for work: adaptive-batch-window + tenant-reserved-capacity options.

jordan (runtime): Putting PR for logging + config guardrails. ETA for review tomorrow.

kai (eng-sre): Will write the RCA template and include metric graphs.

sophie (support): Nice work. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
